To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maternal and starter diets containing long chain n-6 or n-3 PUFA altered tissue tocopherol content in chicks.
the maternal and posthatch diet polyunsaturated fat composition affects tissue tocopherol content in chicks.
maternal and posthatch PUFA diets alter the TOC content in the tissues (liver, plasma) of chicks in early posthatch life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of maternal and posthatch diet PUFA on the TOC status in the early life of chicks.
the effects of maternal and early posthatch dietary PUFA composition on the TOC status in chicks.
the effects of maternal and posthatch diet PUFA on the TOC status in the chick.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
maternal and starter dietary PUFA can alter the tocopherol status (plasma and liver) of chicks during early life.
the maternal and dietary PUFA status of chicks can alter the tocopherol status and that these changes are tissue specific and dependent on the age of the chick.
the maternal and dietary PUFA can affect the tocopherol status in chicks during early life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the n-3 PUFA enriched diet (MO) had the lowest liver TOC status in the hatchlings and the chicks from this diet had the lowest liver (P < 0001), blood (P < 001) and brain (P < 01) TOC status on d 21 posthatching.
the PUFA status of the hen, as well as that of the chick, can influence the TOC content and status of the chick.
the PUFA composition of the diet during incubation and the first week of posthatch can affect the tocopherol status in chicks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maternal and posthatch diets can alter the TOC levels of chicks.
the maternal diet and starter diet PUFAs can affect the TOC levels in liver and plasma of chicks in early posthatch life.
the maternal diet PUFA composition can influence the tocopherol status in the offspring.
